pr.title: Fix search saying No items yet. when nothing matches

findings.what: The message is chosen with a second COUNT(*) query, which adds a DB round trip on every no-match search. The page template also receives a raw HTML string (`empty`) and interpolates it unescaped, so a later caller who passes unescaped text would create an XSS hole.
findings.fix: Optional: pass a flag or plain text and escape it in the template. The current call site does escape `q`.

lenses.note: The change is a small bug fix with one obvious design. The PR's words match the diff, and the failing tests act as the spec.
No spec file is in this change.

Three new tests cover the no-match message, escaping of the search text, and the empty-table case. They would fail against the old code. tests/apply-migrations.js resets the DB before each test, so the DELETE in one test does not leak into others. I could not run `npm test` here because vitest is not installed. CI runs it.
README.md and CLAUDE.md say nothing about the empty-state message, so nothing is stale.
The logic is correct: an empty table gives 'No items yet.', and a search that matches nothing in a non-empty table gives the new message with `q` escaped.
`q` is HTML-escaped in the new message, and a test covers it. SQL is parameterised.
The change adds no UI files. It only changes a text string in the existing server-rendered page.
The change adds no UI files. It only changes a text string in the existing server-rendered page.
The title is under 72 characters. Its claims match the diff: the message is escaped, an empty table still says 'No items yet.', and no tests were deleted or loosened.
